description: docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md:99 says '_rewrite does not catch it', but two functions have that name: the module-level _rewrite (safety/rule_sets.py:583), which never calls guard_spec, and RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite (:859), which does. The sentence also leaves out that run_sql's except Exception turns the error into a fail-closed refusal.
ReferencedByRule stores its two variants as three independent optional fields, and only the _variant validator enforces the exclusive-or, so callers coerce with 'or ""'.
CompareRule.value is typed Any; the scalar-or-list constraint is enforced only in _operand.

LoadedRuleSets.compiled is a public, mutable dict that defaults to empty, and the rule that every row rule has a compiled rule is checked only in guard_spec (which fails closed). GuardSpec.tables is a plain dict next to the MappingProxyType-wrapped rules.

ReferencedByRule stores its two variants as independent optional fields (source_column, source_id_column, link); only the _variant validator enforces mutual exclusion, so downstream code coerces with 'or ""'.
CompareRule.value is typed Any; the scalar-or-non-empty-list rule and the exactly-one-of value/request rule live only in the _operand validator.

LoadedRuleSets.compiled is a public mutable dict defaulting to {}; the every-row-rule-has-a-compiled-rule invariant is checked only in guard_spec (fails closed), and GuardSpec.tables is a plain dict beside the MappingProxyType-wrapped rules.
CompiledRule is frozen but holds a mutable sqlglot condition tree shared by every request; instantiate copies it, but nothing in the type prevents another caller mutating the shared tree in place.

check_catalog now runs first-party logic (VALUE_TYPE_DATA_TYPES lookup, _text decode) after its information_schema reads; any exception from it reaches preflight's blanket except, which tells the operator the check could not read information_schema and to check privileges. Startup is still refused; the diagnosis is misleading.
docs/external/rule-sets.md:264 (Limits) still says 'Rule sets limit which tables and columns a query can read'; with row rules they also limit rows. The line is not in this diff.
rule-sets.md line 5 implies RLS is only one fixed filter for every request; RLS also supports dynamic per-request values.
row-level-security.md line 172 omits row rules when describing rule sets.
Class-sweep sibling (also iter-2 F-6): Limits line said rule sets limit only tables and columns.
